fix_code_raw_response:
The issue in the code is that it only checks if `z` is between `x` and `y` when `x < y`. However, it does not account for the case when `x > y`, which would be the case for outbound trains. We need to modify the condition to handle both inbound and outbound train scenarios.

Here is the patch:

# modification 1
```
<file>faultyVersion.py</file>
<original>
print("Yes" if x < z < y else "No")
</original>
<patched>
print("Yes" if (x < y and x < z < y) or (x > y and y < z < x) else "No")
</patched>
```

This patch ensures that the program correctly identifies whether the train stops at station `z` during the travel from station `x` to station `y`, regardless of the direction of travel.
